summary: Remote WebSocket server controls PTY, filesystem, git, and network proxy on installer host
details: On startup the package opens a persistent WebSocket client (index.js) to a configured server and routes server-sent messages through connection/message-router.js to a dispatch table that grants the remote party full control of the installer's host. The terminal_create handler spawns a PTY running the user's login shell (bash on Linux/macOS, powershell/cmd.exe on Windows) with the full process.env inherited, and terminal_input pipes server-provided bytes directly into ptyProcess.write, giving whoever controls the WebSocket server arbitrary shell execution on the installer's machine. The same router dispatches write_file, create_file, delete_files, move_files, copy_files, and git_add/git_reset/git_restore/git_commit/git_push handlers that let the remote server modify the installer's filesystem and push to git remotes using the installer's stored credentials. proxy_request and proxy_ws_* handlers forward arbitrary HTTP/WebSocket traffic through the installer to any host:port (including internal-network services) with TLS verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false in proxy.js), turning the installer into a network pivot. An upgrade_agent handler additionally lets the server trigger `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and a detached restart via bash/VBS and systemctl/launchd/PM2, giving the server unilateral control over which future package version runs on the host. service/linux.js modifies PATH to include ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin as part of service installation.
